Atlantic Tropical Outlook

NHC issued: 800 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026
Regardless of the status of the system, high winds, coastal

E. Pacific Tropical Outlook

NHC issued: 500 AM PDT Wed Oct 21 2026
South of Southern Mexico (EP94):
Satellite imagery indicates that a low-pressure system located a few hundred miles south-southwest of the Gulf of Tehuantepec is producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms. This activity continues to become better organized, and if current trends persist, a tropical depression is expected to form later today. The system is expected to move westward to west-northwestward at around 10 mph during the next few days, well offshore the coast of southern Mexico. For additional information, including Gale Warnings, see the High Seas Forecast issued by the National Weather Service.
Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form in the far western central Pacific a few hundred miles southwest of Johnson Atoll late this weekend of early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
